title: Remote-first support creates another delay
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
owner_narrative: We visit for simple settings problems, but attempted remote support can also waste 25 minutes before a visit. The remote tool may be absent, the internet down or the caller unauthorized. Customers repeat symptoms to several staff members.

evidence.description: A simulated call records loss of internet before the remote attempt.
A simulated customer policy requires attended access.
A simulated visit repeats checks absent from the ticket.

diagnoses.hypothesis: There is no eligibility gate or structured handover for remote support.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: If remote readiness is high but a hardware replacement is evident, dispatch directly; remote-first is not a universal objective.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Ask connectivity, authorization and symptom questions first; agree a limited remote attempt and a clear escalation point.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Apply a deterministic eligibility checklist; suggest remote or site triage; retain tests, errors and consent references.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Do not initiate control without applicable authorization.
requirements.rationale: There is no eligibility gate or structured handover for remote support.

requirements.statement: Disconnected or obvious physical faults may bypass remote support.
requirements.rationale: There is no eligibility gate or structured handover for remote support.

requirements.statement: Time-box is configured with the service owner, not invented by the model.
requirements.rationale: There is no eligibility gate or structured handover for remote support.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: An offline PC goes to alternative triage without repeated connection attempts.
A failed attempt carries diagnostic notes into dispatch.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Remote eligibility logic is new; remote-control software itself is not provided.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Resolution time by eligibility group; track remote success among eligible cases and extra delay before necessary visits.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Ask connectivity, authorization and symptom questions first; agree a limited remote attempt and a clear escalation point. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: If remote readiness is high but a hardware replacement is evident, dispatch directly; remote-first is not a universal objective.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Approved tools, access policies and practical time-box thresholds need local validation.

transfer_rules.applicable_when: There is no eligibility gate or structured handover for remote support.
transfer_rules.do_not_assume: If remote readiness is high but a hardware replacement is evident, dispatch directly; remote-first is not a universal objective.
